I farm 40 mu under a wheat-maize rotation, so I will use the same 40 mu for winter wheat first and then summer maize after wheat harvest. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on it to keep the crop stable instead of gambling on rainfall. I have been farming for 6 years, so I will keep the plan simple and dependable rather than trying anything complicated. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most of the fertilizer in before or around sowing, irrigate a few key times, and manage weeds and disease with limited but timely spraying. For maize, I will plant hybrid seed because I want stronger yield, use a bit more nitrogen than wheat, keep phosphorus and potassium moderate, and irrigate at the main water-demand stages. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for my wheat-maize system and fits quick turnover between the two crops. I am aiming for solid, realistic yields instead of chasing extreme output.
